channel.title: Ancient Intelligence
channel.description: Elias and Clara investigate the intelligence of the ancient world: mechanical computers, prediction engines, and knowledge systems built on a technological path we never went down, and ask whether reaching artificial intelligence is what ends civilizations. Evidence-anchored: what we know, what is claimed, what we wonder. Follow along on Instagram: @anci.entintelligence

item.title: The Antikythera Mechanism: The Computer That Should Not Exist
item.description:
A hand-cranked bronze computer from a Greek shipwreck: more than thirty gears predicting eclipses and tracking the Moon, a user manual in Greek, Cicero's accounts of similar machines, and the fourteen hundred years before anything like it existed again.

item.title: Göbekli Tepe: The Temple That Rewrote the Timeline
item.description:
Hunter-gatherers raised sixteen-ton carved pillars in southeastern Turkey eleven and a half thousand years ago, before farming, pottery, or writing, and then deliberately buried the place. Klaus Schmidt's discovery, his temple-first thesis, and what it does to the story of civilization.

item.title: Puma Punku: Machining Stone Before the Machine Age
item.description:
Elias and Clara at Puma Punku in Bolivia: the interlocking H blocks, the one hundred and thirty one ton red sandstone slab, the bronze cramps cast in place, Protzen and Nair on the finishing tools archaeology has never found, Posnansky and the seventeen thousand year claim, and the modular design system that died when Tiwanaku fell.
